Definition: middle voice of a derivative of G4177; to behave as a citizen (figuratively):--let conversation be, live.
BiblicalUsage: Politeuomai means to live as a citizen, to conduct yourself by the rules of the city you belong to. Paul says he has lived in all good conscience, and then tells the Philippians to live in a manner worthy of the gospel.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the gospel is not only believed but lived out in public, the way a citizen lives out loyalty to home.
